english.title: Indecent assault on man aged 16 or over
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), indecently assaulted **(..SPECIFY NAME..), a man aged 16 or over
english.legislation: Contrary to section 15(1) of and Schedule 2 to the Sexual Offences Act 1956.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
indecently assaulted
a male person
aged 16 or over

investigatoraction.description: Consider an application for a sexual harm prevention order after conviction

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
THIS OFFENCE IS NOW OBSOLETE

(i) See also offence wordings: H599 and H710 for offences relating to victim under 16 years and under 14 years of age.
(ii) A victim under 16 years of age CANNOT consent to any form of indecent assault, and, since the case of R v K 2000 Times 7.11.00 it has been confirmed that this is an issue of strict liability. Click on the link for section 15(1) (in legislation above) and read the notes for more.
(iii) This offence is included in Schedule 1(1) to the Sex Offenders Act 1997, therefore a person convicted or cautioned for this offence must (subject to the exceptions and provisions contained in Schedule 1(2) and (3)) comply with the requirements of section 2 of that Act.
(iv) Repealed by s.140 of and Schedule 7 to the Sexual Offences Act 2003

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Ten years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
